text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows two applications to communicate by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to specific endpoints. Usually, the server responds with data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access most APIs, you need authentication, often through an API key or token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, because network problems or invalid requests can happen at any time.
